reason: Neither conversation asked for the model label or the pulsing-vs-clean-stop question, and neither pointed the homeowner to Dyson support, so both fell short on the sensible first steps. Conversation 1 nonetheless stayed honest: it checked the charger contacts (an acceptable direction), identified a worn battery as 'most likely' while explicitly declining to confirm or recommend a part, though its final turn was unhelpful and its 'appliance engineer' escalation was the wrong route. Conversation 2 was more engaged and proposed a useful timed-run test, but it opened by re-suggesting a blockage/damp filter (already ruled out, no pulsing) and closed by declaring the battery 'effectively confirmed' and telling the owner to 'proceed with the battery replacement' without ever establishing the model, both of which are listed unsupported claims that risk a wasted £60+ purchase.
